scope.rule: This section defines procedures, formulas, tables, and constraints for creating new monsters within ACKS-compatible ranges.
A created monster is finalized by tabulating a monster listing and adding a short appearance, behavior, and habitat summary, but only the mechanical generation rules are summarized here.

creation_procedure.step: Choose one or more monster types.
Determine saving throws from monster type and hit dice.
Determine weight in pounds using weight = (hd × 10)^bme.
Determine normal load in stone using normal_load = weight × ccf.
Determine armor class from hit dice, body form modifier, and size modifier.
Choose natural attacks from body form and modify as desired.
Assign damage so the full attack routine averages about 2 hp per hd.
Choose movement rate from body form.
Calculate xp value from hit dice and counted special abilities.
Determine typical dungeon and wilderness encounters.
Determine treasure type from average treasure value and accumulation method.
Optionally calculate taming and training characteristics.

general_rules.rule: A creature may belong to multiple types.
Monster type determines charm, hold, protection, detection, sleep, and similar spell interactions, saving throw progression, and number of special abilities.
Constructs are also enchanted creatures for purposes of spells such as dispel evil and protection from evil.
Undead constructs such as skeletons and zombies count as both undead and construct.
Summoned creatures of Chaotic alignment are inherently evil for detect evil and protection from evil.
Undead are inherently evil for detect evil and protection from evil.

Variant saving throw progressions may be assigned instead of fighter at Judge discretion: cleric for divine spellcasting or divine spell-like powers, mage for arcane spellcasting or arcane spell-like powers, thief for thief-like abilities or stealth/ambush focus, dwarf or elf only for creatures closely akin to those races.

type.name: animal
type.rule: Includes real-world sub-human creatures, giant normal animals, and prehistoric animals.
Charm animal, speak with animal, and related magic items work on animals.
Animals are also vulnerable to charm monster and hold monster.

type.name: beastman
type.rule: Created by ancient magic blending humanoids with animals or fantastic creatures.

type.name: construct
type.rule: Mindless, unliving monsters.
Immune to gas and poison.
Unaffected by charm, sleep, and hold.

type.name: enchanted_creature
type.rule: Can be kept at bay by protection from evil and destroyed or driven off by dispel evil.

type.name: fantastic_creature
type.rule: Characterized by magical powers, impossible body-part combinations, or both.
Not affected by charm person or hold person.
Usually vulnerable to charm monster and hold monster.

type.name: giant_humanoid
type.rule: Creatures that would be humanoids except for great size and 5 or more hd.
Not affected by charm person or hold person.
Vulnerable to charm monster and hold monster.

type.name: humanoid
type.rule: No larger than an ogre and possessing 4 or fewer hd.
Humans and demi-humans remain humanoids even above 4 hd or level 4.
All humanoids are vulnerable to charm person and hold person.

type.name: ooze
type.rule: Mindless monsters with varied immunities and vulnerabilities.
All oozes are immune to charm, hold, and sleep.

type.name: summoned_creature
type.rule: Can be kept at bay by protection from evil and destroyed or driven off by dispel evil.
Usually vulnerable to charm monster and hold monster.

type.name: undead
type.rule: Immune to gas and poison.
Unaffected by charm, sleep, or hold of any sort.
Usually silent in movement.

type.name: vermin
type.rule: Lower life forms with minimal intelligence.
Cannot be affected by spells that affect animals.
Usually vulnerable to charm monster and hold monster.

row.immunities: charm, hold, sleep, gas, poison, various
charm, hold, sleep, gas, poison, various

general_rules.rule: Body form determines natural attacks, movement, armor class modifier, weight scaling, carrying capacity factor, and influences organization and intelligence tables.
A hybrid body form may use movement from either or both forms. Using both movement sets counts as a special ability.
A hybrid body form uses the ac modifier of the form whose movement it uses. If it uses both movement sets, use the better ac modifier.
A hybrid body form may use attacks from either or both forms. Using both attack sets counts as a special ability.
A hybrid body form may use bme and ccf from either body form or a mid-range value between them.

draconine_special_rule.rule: Draconine armor class is +2 + 1/2 per hd up to 20 hd.

hit_dice_rules.rule: Hit dice measure fighting ability and toughness.
Normal range runs from less than 1 hd to 36 hd or more.
Hit dice affect hit points, size category, armor class, attack throws, saving throws, damage, experience value, and treasure type.

bonus_hit_points.rule: Printed hd bonuses such as 1+1 or 4+2 count as bonus hit points.
Each bonus point counts as 0.25 hd for weight, armor class, carrying capacity, and damage calculations.

general_size_rules.rule: Wingspan of flying creatures is typically three times length.

square_cube_law_optional.rule: Optional adjusted carrying capacity = (baseline monster ccf × new monster weight) × ((new monster weight / baseline monster weight)^(2/3) / (new monster weight / baseline monster weight)).
Use this primarily when the new creature is one or more size categories larger than typical for its body form.

armor_class.rule: Base ac increases by 0.8 per hd for the first 9 hd only.
Round to the nearest whole number, rounding 0.5 up if odd and down if even.
Apply size category ac modifier unless body form says otherwise.
Species variation may adjust ac by -1, 0, or +1; roll 1d6 or choose: 1-2 = -1, 3-4 = +0, 5-6 = +1.

size_hit_dice_limits.rule: These limits apply to unnaturally tough monsters in the absence of magic.
Enchanted creatures and undead may ignore these size-based maximum hd limits.

unnaturally_tough_monsters.rule: Weight, carrying capacity, and size may be calculated from a lower hd value than the one used for hit points, attack throws, ac, damage, saving throws, xp, and treasure type.
The same process can be reversed to create unnaturally weak monsters.

general_rules.rule: Recommended attacks come from body form, but the Judge may add, remove, or modify them.
Attack throws are determined by hit dice using normal monster attack throw rules.
A monster's full attack sequence should average about 2 hp damage per hd.
That damage may be divided across attacks as desired.
The natural attack damage table is guidance, not a mandatory formula.
Monsters using normal weapons inflict average damage equal to 2.5 + 1 hp per full hd.
Adjust weapon damage up or down for unusually small or large weapons.
A monster may have zero to five special abilities in addition to monster-type immunities.
The Judge may choose the number or roll using the monster type table.
Roll or choose each special ability from the special abilities table.
Re-roll duplicate abilities unless the result explicitly permits stacking or converting a duplicate into immunity.
All results are cumulative.
Some abilities modify attacks, damage, movement, or ac; update derived values after assignment.
The Judge may alter the text, balance, or exact implementation of listed abilities.

xp_counting_rules.rule: Major abilities are marked with one or more asterisks.
Minor abilities are marked with one or more hashtags.
Round counted abilities to the nearest whole number, rounding .5 down if even and up if odd.
Record that total beside hd as the monster's counted special abilities for xp.

spell_like_ability_counting.rule: Each spell-like ability counts as minor abilities equal to 2 × spell_level × usage_factor.

special_disabilities.rule: Each special disability may permit one additional special ability, up to the normal maximum for the monster's type.
A disability may also reduce counted asterisks if it meaningfully weakens the creature or fully offsets a strong ability.
special_disabilities.sample_disability: Hateful towards a particular creature type and attacks on sight regardless of circumstances.
Instantly killed by an ordinary spell effect or condition; counts as 2 disabilities.
Rendered dormant by an otherwise ordinary condition.
Sensitive to a common environmental condition and suffers -1d3 attack penalty.
Substantial movement reduction or loss of the special movement capability typical for its body type.
Vulnerable to a particular attack type and suffers double damage or loses normal immunity or resistance.
Vulnerable to a particular attack type and is paralyzed for one round per die of damage that attack deals.

ability.name: acid
ability.rule: Monster attacks destroy non-magical armor or clothing on a successful hit.
A non-magical weapon striking the monster dissolves immediately after dealing damage.
Magical weapons and armor receive a saving throw using the wearer's save versus death, adding magical bonus if applicable.

ability.name: aura
ability.rule: The monster has a damaging aura with radius 2' per hd.
The aura deals 1d8 damage per round to susceptible creatures.

ability.name: berserk
ability.rule: +2 bonus to attack rolls.
Immune to fear.
Morale becomes +4.

ability.name: bonus_attack
ability.rule: Roll 1d6.

row.result: one bonus attack dealing damage equal to primary attack
two bonus attacks each dealing damage equal to secondary attack or half the primary attack

ability.rule: If average damage exceeds 4 points per hd, the ability counts as *; otherwise it counts as ##.

ability.name: breath_weapon
ability.rule: Usable 3/day.
Deals 1d6 damage per hd.
Save versus blast halves damage.
Area and special properties are as per a dragon.

ability.name: charge
ability.rule: Choose one natural attack type.
Charge attacks with that attack type deal double damage.

ability.name: charm
ability.rule: Usable 3/day or by gaze.
Target must save versus spells or become totally enthralled.
If monster has 3 hd or less, targets save at +2.
If monster has 9 hd or more, targets save at -2.

ability.name: class_powers_or_proficiencies
ability.rule: Monster gains 1d4 class powers or proficiencies chosen to fit design, excluding spellcasting.
If the monster gains all powers of a class, the result counts as *.
Otherwise each class power counts as one #.

ability.name: energy_drain
ability.rule: Victims of the primary attack lose experience levels.
If monster has 6 hd or less, it drains 1 level.
If monster has 7 hd or more, it drains 2 levels.

ability.name: flying
ability.rule: If the monster cannot already fly, it gains flight at exploration movement equal to twice base movement.
If it already flies, it gains dive attacks that deal double damage.
If a dive hits a victim smaller than the monster, the victim is grabbed and carried off unless he saves versus paralysis.
If the monster already has a dive attack, re-roll this result.

ability.name: grab
ability.rule: Victims of the primary attack save versus paralysis or are grabbed.
Grabbed victims are helpless until they escape by succeeding on a saving throw versus paralysis on their turn.

ability.name: hug
ability.rule: If the monster hits with more than half of its attacks in an attack sequence, it deals extra damage.

ability.name: immunity
ability.rule: Re-roll if the monster is already immune to the rolled effect.

ability.name: incorporeal
ability.rule: Monster is formless, weightless, and cannot interact with physical objects except through its attacks or special abilities.
If 4 hd or less, it can only be harmed by silver weapons.
If 5 hd or more, it can only be harmed by magical weapons.
It may select energy drain and flying as special abilities.

ability.name: infectious
ability.rule: Victims may transform into others of the monster's kind.
Creatures slain by the monster may rise as that monster type unless appropriate measures are taken.
Alternatively, victims suffering loss of half or more of their hit points to the monster's natural attacks may transform after 2d6 days.

ability.name: initiative
ability.rule: The monster always has initiative each round.

ability.name: invisibility
ability.rule: The monster is naturally invisible.
It may act freely, including attacking, without becoming visible.

ability.name: magic_resistance
ability.rule: Magic resistance target value = 20 - hd.

ability.name: ongoing_damage
ability.rule: Once the monster has hit its victim, it deals ongoing damage each round equal to its most damaging attack.
Special effects such as poison or energy drain are not ongoing unless separately specified.

ability.name: paralysis
ability.rule: Victims of primary attack(s) save versus paralysis or are paralyzed.

ability.name: petrification
ability.rule: Roll 1d6.

row.result: save versus petrification or turn to stone

row.trigger: being struck by the monster's attacks
row.result: save versus petrification or turn to stone

ability.name: poison
ability.rule: Victims of primary attack(s) save versus poison or die.
If monster has 3 hd or less, save is at +2.
If monster has 9 hd or more, save is at -2.

ability.name: regeneration
ability.rule: Monster regenerates hd/2 hit points per round.
Lost limbs can be re-attached.
Regeneration does not function against two specific damage types, usually fire and acid.

ability.name: resistance
ability.rule: The monster gains resistance to two effects.
If the same effect is rolled twice, the monster instead becomes immune to it.
Re-roll if the monster is already immune to the effect.

ability.name: spellcasting
ability.rule: Monster casts as a classed character with level equal to hd, maximum 14th level.

ability.name: spell_like_abilities
ability.rule: Monster gains 1d4 spell-like abilities.
Generate as if rolling for spell scrolls or choose abilities that fit existing powers.
Each counts using the spell-like ability counting formula.

row.result: characters encountering the monster at any time suffer -1 to surprise rolls
characters encountering the monster in its natural habitat suffer -1 to surprise rolls
characters encountering the monster in its natural habitat suffer -2 to surprise rolls

ability.name: swallow_attack
ability.rule: On an unmodified attack throw of 19 or 20, the monster swallows whole a victim smaller than itself.
A swallowed victim takes damage equal to the monster's most damaging attack each round until either the monster is killed or the victim dies.

ability.name: swift
ability.rule: Movement rate increases by 30' for every 120' of base encounter movement.

ability.name: terrifying
ability.rule: Any being seeing the monster saves versus paralysis or is paralyzed with dread.
The effect ends if the monster leaves the victim's line of sight or engages in combat.

ability.name: tough
ability.rule: Ac increases by 1d4 points.
If this raises ac to more than hd × 1.5, it counts as *.
Otherwise it counts as ##.

ability.name: trample
ability.rule: The monster gains a trample attack usable instead of its normal attack sequence.
The trample attack should average 2 hp damage per hd.
The monster gains +4 to attack man-sized targets when trampling.
If the monster is not at least large size, re-roll.

ability.name: unusual
ability.rule: Judge assigns a rare, unique, or special power.

general_rule.rule: Monster xp = base xp for hd + (bonus xp per counted ability × number of counted abilities).

experience_points.rule: For monsters of hd 22 and higher, add a cumulative 250 xp to both base xp and bonus xp per ability for each hd above 21.

general_rules.rule: Typical encounter format is [collective noun] (number encountered) / [collective noun] (number encountered).
The first part is an encounter outside the lair; the second part is inside the lair.
If a monster does not make a lair, list only one collective noun and range.
If the monster is not found in dungeon or wilderness, list none.
% in lair ranges from none to 100%; average is 25%.
Organization table values are expressed as average total hit dice of encounters.
Monsters whose hd exceed the recommended total hd for a listed encounter are usually solitary (1).
Average treasure value = 4 × monster xp value × average number encountered in its dungeon lair.
If the monster has no dungeon lair, use its wilderness lair instead.
Determine whether treasure is accumulated by hoarding, raiding, or accident.
Cross-reference average treasure value and accumulation method to determine treasure type.
Treasure value may be adjusted up or down by one or more rows if the monster should have more or less treasure than usual for its hd.

animal_intelligence_by_body_form.rule: Animal-intelligence monsters use trainability modifier and training period from body form.
The Judge may modify these values.

general_rules.rule: Alignment is restricted by monster type and intelligence, but the Judge may overrule these restrictions.
Animals are generally Neutral, sometimes Lawful, never Chaotic.
Beastmen are typically Chaotic, occasionally Neutral, almost never Lawful.
Enchanted creatures and fantastic creatures may be any alignment; if animal or mindless they are typically Neutral but may be Lawful or Chaotic.
Humanoids and giant humanoids may be any alignment.
Oozes and vermin are typically Neutral; some may be Chaotic.
Summoned creatures may be Neutral or Chaotic, never Lawful.
Undead are always Chaotic.

lifespan_rules.rule: Maximum lifespan may be determined in any of three ways.

method.name: weight_formula
method.rule: High-brain-mass creatures, birds, and reptiles tend to live longer than this estimate.

method.name: known_lifespan
method.rule: If the source concept has a known or reputed lifespan, that value may be used directly.

trained_value.rule: Trained value in gp = monthly wage × 33.
If detailed battle rating wage rules are unavailable, estimate trained value as (ac + 1) × hd × (hd + 1) × (1 + number_of_counted_special_abilities) × 24.
Only special abilities that warrant an asterisk count for this formula.
Round values of 10,000gp or less to nearest 100gp.

other_value_modifiers.rule: These percentages approximate values from trained adult price.
Round using the same thresholds as trained value.
Actual published values may vary widely because the full calculation uses a more complex spreadsheet.
